outcome.answer: Yes. ArcGD is a geometry-inspired optimizer that, on a highly non-convex Rosenbrock benchmark, consistently outperformed Adam under one matched-learning-rate setting and achieved superior final solutions in most cases under another [1]. EISAM is also geometry-based in the sense of using a prediction step that investigates the loss landscape, and it consistently outperformed Adam in test accuracy and training efficiency across benchmark datasets [6].
